title: New `zoom <z>` demo directive has zero test coverage (parse guard, normalization, run_demo application)
evidence: demo.odin: `z, okz := strconv.parse_f32(fields[1])` / `if !okz || !(z >= 1.0 && z <= 4.0) { // the NaN-rejecting band test (z < 1.0 is false for NaN)` / `return {}, fmt.tprintf("bad zoom %q (want 1.0..4.0 — the camera band): %s", fields[1], line)` / `d.zoom = z`; demo.odin:693: `d.zoom = 1.0`; run.odin: `rnd.view_refit(&rc.view)` ... `rc.view.zoom_rung = rnd.zoom_rung_of(zoom)` / `if zoom != 1.0 {`. Grep proof: `grep -rn "^zoom" demos/` = 0 hits; no harness test file references zoom (harness has only a11y_oracle_test.odin's 2 tests); palcheck sets `view.zoom_rung = rnd.zoom_rung_of(z)` directly, never through this path.
detail: The L2 story's new directive ships untested: NaN/band rejection, absent→fit normalization, and the run_demo transform block have no unit test and no demo exercises them, so all-golden-green proves nothing about this code.
recommended_fix: Add harness unit tests: parse accepts 1.0/4.0, rejects NaN/0.9/4.1/non-numeric; absent normalizes to 1.0; run_demo applies scale=fit*z with the derived rung (assert view.scale and zoom_rung).

title: App camera_update's rung wiring (the live player camera path) is untested
evidence: app/main.odin:1894: `v.zoom_rung = rnd.zoom_rung_of(app.cam_zoom)`. Grep proof: `zoom_rung` appears in NO app test file (only look_l1/l2/l4_test in app/render, which set `v.zoom_rung` directly); harness/run.odin derives the rung itself (`rc.view.zoom_rung = rnd.zoom_rung_of(zoom)`), so goldens never execute camera_update's line; palcheck sets the field manually (`view.zoom_rung = rnd.zoom_rung_of(z)`).
detail: Deleting this line fails nothing: unit tests, palcheck, and goldens all bypass camera_update. The only consumer where the rung rides the LIVE eased camera — the primary player surface — has no regression pin.
recommended_fix: Add an app test: set cam_zoom above/below the cuts, call camera_update, assert v.zoom_rung == zoom_rung_of(cam_zoom) (covers the 1.6/1.25 boundaries through the real path).

title: wire_path_test exercises wire_paths_compute only at cap-0 width and pins the retired uncapped band_world basis
evidence: wire_path_test.odin:36: `v.sprites.ok = false` (test_view does `v^ = {}` — bboxes zero, never hand-set). wire_path.odin:609: `band := link_width_capped(v, topo, bundles, u32(bi))`. wire_path_test.odin:222 and 305: `band := band_world(&v, s.bundles.bundle_tier[bi], int(s.bundles.bundle_count[bi]))`. look_l1_test.odin names the class: `WITHOUT these, sprite_puck_target computes min(0/110, 1.30) = 0 and every ROUTER endpoint's drawn size — and with it the covenant cap — silently zeroes`. wire_paths_compute callers in tests: only lines 127, 188-189 (cost-immunity/determinism — no width assertion).
detail: Every fixture bundle touches a router, so zero bboxes make the covenant cap 0 and wire_paths_compute runs at band 0 — the same vacuity the PR fixed in look_l1 persists here; the two direct-call tests compute against the uncapped basis production abandoned.
recommended_fix: Hand-set puck bboxes in test_view (the look_l1_set_puck_bboxes pattern), switch lines 222/305 to link_width_capped, and assert wire_paths_compute's band equals the capped width.

title: Covenant consumer reversion (outline, halos, rider lattice, assist glow) is unpinned — the bug class step-04 caught can recur silently
evidence: crisis.odin:390: `band := link_width_capped(v, topo, bundles, b) * v.scale`; view.odin:2272: `halo := link_width_capped(v, topo, bundles, bi) * v.scale + 6 * v.scale`; assist.odin:425: `halo := link_width_capped(v, topo, bundles, bi) * v.scale + 6.0 * v.scale`. The only width pins are the stroke itself: palcheck.odin:674 `check(abs(runs - expected) <= 1.0,` and the L1 unit tests over link_width_capped. PR body: "the crisis OUTLINE still drew the UNCAPPED width (the halo/selection/riders were migrated, the outline missed) → link_width_capped threaded".
detail: No test asserts a consumer's width — a revert of outline/selection/congestion/rider/assist to uncapped band_width passes every unit test, and goldens only catch it if a clamped fat bundle happens to sit in a blessed crisis frame.
recommended_fix: Extend palcheck's crisis section: render a clamped fat bundle in crisis, measure the outline run, assert it equals the capped stroke (+4+5·factor), not link_width_world.
